body:
Two more from a second walkthrough pass, both generic renderer behaviour rather than app metadata.

## 9. A `colorField` view colours its records and never says what the colours mean

`crm_event`'s calendar view declares:

```ts
type: 'calendar',
titleField: 'subject',
colorField: 'type',     // 电话 / 会议 / 演示 / 线上研讨会
```

and the month grid duly renders each event in a colour derived from its type — amber for one, pink for another, and so on. There is **no legend anywhere on the view**: no key in the toolbar, no swatch row under the grid, nothing in the DOM (`[class*=legend]` matches nothing; the only type word on the page is the one inside a subject line).

So the encoding is real and unreadable. A user sees two colours and has no way to learn that one means *webinar* and the other *demo* short of opening records one at a time and correlating. The same `colorField` is declared on the timeline view, with the same result.

Wherever a view declares `colorField`, the renderer knows both the field and its option labels — it already resolves them to pick the colours. Emitting a legend (toolbar chip row, or a collapsible key beside the view switcher) is the missing half, and no app author can add it declaratively.

Related but separable: when the coloured field is a picklist with declared option colours, the legend should use those rather than a derived palette, so the calendar agrees with the badge colours the same values get in list views.

## 10. Calendar event titles truncate before the distinguishing part

Month cells render `Wayne — pla…`, `Acme — re…`, `Vertex — e…`. The pills have roughly 60% of the cell width and the text is cut at ~12 characters, which in practice lands right where the events stop being identical — every title in this dataset is `{Account} — {what}`, so the truncation preserves the redundant half and drops the informative one.

Two cheap improvements, independent of each other: let the pill use the cell's full width before truncating, and put the full subject in a `title`/tooltip (it is already there on the wrapper — moving it onto the text element would make hovering the label work). Middle-truncation (`Wayne — …webinar`) would beat trailing truncation for this shape, as it does for the breadcrumbs in item 7.
